articles.title: 7 regulated payment activities
articles.requirement: Licence required for any of: (a) account-issuance service; (b) domestic money-transfer service; (c) cross-border money-transfer service; (d) merchant-acquisition service; (e) e-money issuance service; (f) digital payment token service (DPT); (g) money-changing service. A licensee may be authorised for multiple activities; activity scope drives capital + AML + safeguarding obligations.

articles.title: Licensing tiers — MC / SPI / MPI
articles.requirement: Three tiers based on activity + scale: (a) Money-Changing licence (money-changing only); (b) Standard Payment Institution (SPI) — for limited-scale providers (monthly transaction threshold-based); (c) Major Payment Institution (MPI) — for high-volume providers above threshold. Capital, AML, safeguarding obligations scale with tier; DPT activities typically MPI tier due to risk profile.

articles.title: DPT service — pre-2024 framework
articles.requirement: DPT service (since 2020) covers: dealing in DPTs (buying / selling DPTs against money or other DPTs); facilitating DPT exchange (operating an exchange platform); accepting custody, control or possession of DPTs belonging to another person; facilitating DPT transmission. Triggers full AML/CFT + technology-risk + safeguarding obligations.

articles.title: DPT user-protection expansion (April 2024 amendments)
articles.requirement: New user-protection requirements effective 4 April 2024: customer-asset segregation (separation of customer DPTs from own holdings); custody safeguards (insolvency-remote arrangements + secure custody); pre-contract risk disclosures (volatility + loss + investor-protection limitations); ban on offering retail credit for DPT purchase; prohibition on incentivising DPT trading (loyalty rewards, referral bonuses); marketing restrictions targeting retail audiences.

articles.title: Safeguarding of customer money (SPI / MPI)
articles.requirement: MPI for account-issuance + money-transfer + e-money issuance must safeguard customer money via approved mechanisms: (a) safeguarding account with a safeguarding institution; (b) safeguarding undertaking (e.g. guarantee from a safeguarding institution); (c) insurance covering the customer money. Daily reconciliation + reporting required. Customer protection in MPI insolvency.

articles.title: Safeguarding of customer DPTs
articles.requirement: DPT service providers holding customer DPTs must segregate customer DPTs from own holdings; maintain insolvency-remote arrangements; implement secure custody (cold + hot wallet structure proportionate to risk; key-management; multi-party computation or HSM-style controls where appropriate); reporting of customer-asset balances to MAS on prescribed cadence.

articles.title: AML/CFT obligations — MAS Notice PSN01 + PSN02
articles.requirement: All PSA licensees subject to AML/CFT obligations under MAS Notice PSN01 (for non-DPT payment service providers) + PSN02 (for DPT service providers). Structure mirrors MAS Notice 626: entity-wide risk assessment with PF dimension (post-30 June 2025); CDD + EDD; PEPs; STR to STRO; sanctions screening; tipping-off prohibition; internal policies + training + record retention.

articles.title: Technology + cybersecurity
articles.section: MAS TRM Guidelines + Notice on Cyber Hygiene
articles.requirement: PSA licensees subject to MAS TRM Guidelines proportionate to scale + risk + activity: technology-risk governance; cybersecurity (incl. wallet + key management for DPT); IT-incident management; cloud + IT third-party management; data centre + system availability. MAS Notice on Cyber Hygiene mandates baseline cyber controls (admin-access controls, vulnerability management, security patches, MFA, account lockout).

articles.title: Outsourcing — MAS Outsourcing Guidelines
articles.requirement: Outsourcing arrangements subject to MAS Outsourcing Guidelines: pre-contract due diligence on the service provider; written contract with required minimums (access, audit, security, exit, sub-outsourcing); ongoing monitoring + reporting of material issues; notification to MAS for material outsourcings; exit-strategy planning. Updated 2024 to reflect cloud-specific + AI-vendor specific expectations.

articles.title: Enforcement
articles.requirement: MAS enforcement under PSA includes: civil + criminal sanctions for unlicensed operation; licence suspension or revocation; civil monetary penalties for breaches; prohibition orders against directors / key officers; remediation orders. Enforcement actions published with names + facts via MAS Enforcement Reports + media releases — significant reputational consequence.
